text: Company is, in truth, a constant state of negotiation; and, if you attend to it in that view, will qualify you for any. By the same means that you make a friend, guard against an enemy, or gain a mistress; you will make an advantageous treaty, baffle those who counteract you, and gain the court you are sent to.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter CLXXVIII, to his son, London, September 26, 1752
